test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What does the term ‘Catch-all’ mean?

options.text: A category which includes all the types of media
A category that includes all the sources of information
A category that includes all the sources of entertainment
A category which includes many different things

solution:
The correct answer is** Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term** "catch-all" **is typically used **to describe a category or term that encompasses a wide variety of items or concepts. **
 
• In the passage, **"new media"** is described **as a catch-all term for various types of electronic communications**.
 
• This implies that** "new media" **includes **a broad range of media forms without being limited to a specific type**.
 
• **The term does not specify any particular type of media, source of information, or source of entertainment, but rather includes all possible variations.**
 
• The passage highlights that **"new media"** consists of diverse components like **websites, online forums, blogs, and more.**
 
• The description aligns with the** idea of a category that embraces many different things, reflecting the diverse nature of new media.**

Conclusion: Therefore, the correct answer is** 'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** A category which includes all the types of media: **This option is too restrictive and specific, focusing only on media types.
 
• **A category that includes all the sources of information: **This is also too narrow, concentrating solely on information sources.
 
• **A category that includes all the sources of entertainment: **This limits the scope to entertainment, which is not what the term "catch-all" implies in the passage.
